task: Two robustness gaps in this orchestrator. (1) CLI errors must be clean: running 'python3 -m autopilot lint|lock|run|plan|review' with a --repo path that does not exist or is not a git repository, or with a plan file that is missing or not valid JSON, must print a single line starting with 'FAIL ' to stdout and exit 2, never a Python traceback. (2) canary_for() in autopilot/judge.py must handle compound judge commands: split judge.cmd on '&&', '||' and ';', derive the canary from the first segment that is a recognised 'unittest discover' or pytest-on-a-directory invocation, and ignore -s/-p/-k tokens that belong to the other segments. The existing suite runs with 'python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .' and must stay green.

global.constraints: One branch carries both items in order. Do not edit judge.paths files (tests/test_cli_errors.py, tests/test_canary_compound.py, tests/helpers.py). No new dependencies. The existing suite 'python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .' must stay green after each item (after item 1 it is red only on tests/test_canary_compound.py until item 2 lands). Keep stdout 'FAIL ' format and exit code 2 as already used by lint problems.

items.goal: lint, lock, run, review and plan print one 'FAIL ...' line on stdout and exit 2 (no traceback) for a nonexistent --repo, a non-git --repo, a missing plan file, or a plan file that is not valid JSON

target.state: proven (tests/test_cli_errors.py is red today: ran and failed)

items.interfaces: CLI contract only: stdout exactly one line starting 'FAIL ', exit code 2, stderr free of 'Traceback'. Prefer a single guard in main() around args.fn (catch FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError, NotADirectoryError, gitx's git-failure exception, and validate --repo is an existing git work tree before dispatch) rather than per-command try blocks. Do not change exit codes 0/1/3/4 for other paths.
items.notes: Valid-but-bad-argument cases only; the 'report' command is not in scope. The tests use a plan built from tests/helpers.py, so helpers.py is locked.

items.goal: canary_for() splits judge.cmd on '&&', '||' and ';', derives the canary from the first segment that is a recognised 'unittest discover' or pytest-on-a-directory invocation, and ignores -s/-p/-k tokens belonging to other segments

target.value: 8 compound-canary tests green and the full existing suite green
target.state: proven (test_canary_compound is red today: 5 of 8 cases fail; full suite green before this change)

items.interfaces: canary_for(item, checkout) -> tuple[Path, str] | None keeps its signature. Explicit judge.canary still wins. A -k inside the chosen segment still returns None; -k elsewhere does not. No recognised segment -> None. Single-segment commands behave exactly as before.
items.notes: Split must respect quoting (e.g. -p 'a;b*.py' should not split inside quotes); a shlex-based tokenizer with punctuation_chars or a quote-aware splitter both work. This judge depends on item 1 being merged because the full suite includes tests/test_cli_errors.py.

judge.cmd: python3 -m unittest tests.test_canary_compound && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

next_rung: Make compound-command handling shared: have lint/judge parse judge commands into segments once (also catching `cd sub && ...` working-directory changes and `a&&b` without spaces), and give the CLI a typed error class (e.g. CliError) so every command, including `report`, reports user mistakes uniformly instead of the single guard in main().
